# Define projection

```{r, ROMS.test}

# Since the data falls within two UTM zones and there is not an ideal projection to use, apply a custom equal area Albers projection
aea_custom <- "+proj=aea +lat_1=30 +lat_2=50 +lat_0=40 +lon_0=-124.5 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"


```

# Create plot gradicule labels

Note this is only for graph labels and is chosen based on the mean lat and lon values of the haul transect locations.

```{r, Create.plot.label.breaks}

lat_breaks <- seq(27, 55, 4)  # Latitude breaks

lat_labels <- c(paste(27, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(31, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(35, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(39, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(43, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(47, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(51, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""),
                paste(55, "\u00b0", "N", sep=""))

```

# Create base map

Note that cropping should be done before projecting the data and projecting the data should be done before any intersection analysis.

```{r, basemap}


# 1. Turn off s2 processing for map graphic only
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Make coastline backdrop
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------

PacificCoast <- ne_countries(scale = 10, returnclass = "sf") 
PacificCoast3.wgs84 <- st_crop(PacificCoast, xmin = -133, xmax = -110, 
                               ymin = 25, 
                         ymax = 55)
class(PacificCoast3.wgs84)

#---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot output
#---------------------------------------------------------------------------

ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = PacificCoast3.wgs84, fill = "#D2B48C", col = "#927143") +
    xlab("Longitude") + ylab("Latitude") +
    ggtitle("West Coast map") +
    theme_classic()

```

```{r, adjust.map.dimensions}
  st_crop(PacificCoast3.wgs84, 
          xmin = -133, 
          xmax = -111,
          ymin = 27, 
          ymax = 55)
  
#----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot
#----------------------------------------------------------------------------

PacificCoast.wgs84.map <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = PacificCoast.wgs84,
          color = "#ae8f60",

  theme_void() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(27,55),

PacificCoast.wgs84.map

st_bbox(PacificCoast.wgs84)

# For plot intersection work, transform to Albers equal area
PacificCoast.aea_custom <- st_transform(PacificCoast.wgs84, crs = aea_custom)

```

# Create city markers

To make the map easier to interpret, add the names and locations of most populated cites

```{r, add.map.details}

# 1. Turn off s2 processing for map graphic only
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

#----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# populated areas (cities and city names)
#----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Populated10.wgs84 <- ne_download(scale = 110, type = "populated_places_simple", 
                           category = "cultural", 
                           returnclass = "sf") 

# For plot intersection work, transform to Albers equal area
Populated10.aea_custom <- Populated10.wgs84 |>
  st_transform(crs = aea_custom)

Populated10 <- st_intersection(Populated10.aea_custom, PacificCoast.aea_custom)

```

# Prepare survey data structure

```{r, adapt.survey.structure}

# 1. Turn on s2 processing for map graphic only
sf_use_s2(TRUE)

TwoSeas.dat2 <- fread(
  here(dir, "Data", "Canada.and.CPS.ATM.Survey.Data.w.latBin.csv"))
# View(TwoSeas.dat2)

# Check how many keys are present in 
# the ROMS hindcast
test.keys <- TwoSeas.dat2 |> 
  filter(Year < 2021) 
length(unique(test.keys$keys))
# [1] 3249

# Create transect data
## Rename columns to match function 
survey.transects.sf <- TwoSeas.dat2 |>
  group_by(keys) |> 
  # remove potentially conflicting column names
  select(-c(X,Y)) |>
  mutate(FID = keys) |>
  make_transect_sf(crs = 4326) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # Project the data to Albers Conical Equal Area
  st_transform(crs = aea_custom) |>
  group_by(Year, Season, latBin, keys, YearSeas.nm) |>
  mutate(Haul.kg = round(sum(Scaled_Biomass_Contribution), 7),
            Haul.check = first(Species_weight),
            Fin_sweep.m3 = first(Fin_sweep.m3)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(Year, Season, latBin, keys, YearSeas.nm, len.bin) |>
  mutate(Haul_Bin.kg = round(sum(Scaled_Biomass_Contribution), 7)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(Month = month(date)) |>
  mutate(survey_date = as.Date(paste0(Year, "-", Month, "-01"))) |>
  ungroup()

```

# CDO regridding of MLD

To see how the regridding of the ROMS data works, run the following:

```{r, test.mld.def}

# 1. Turn on s2 processing for map graphic only
sf_use_s2(TRUE)

# File path
nc_file.mld2 <- here(dir, "Data", "ROMS2", "Regridded",
                     "mld_hindcast_2019_masked_regrid.nc")

# Open the NetCDF file
nc.mld2 <- nc_open(nc_file.mld2)

# Get all variable names
var_names2 <- names(nc.mld2$var)
var_names2
# [1] "mld"

# Note that we forced the values in the workaround so it is actually not a 
## curvilinear grid any more
st.mld2 <- read_stars(nc_file.mld2, curvilinear = NULL)

# Manually reset the dimensions to the meter-based values stars often 
## struggles with curvilinear-to-rectilinear conversion on read-in
st.mld2 <- st_set_crs(st.mld2, aea_custom)

# Check if meta data is conserved
attributes(st.mld2)$units

# Often meta data will not be conserved and you will need to manually assign it
attr(st.mld2[[1]], "units") <- nc.mld2$var$mld$units

# Check that it is saved
attr(st.mld2[[1]], "units")

# Assuming dims: var_data[time, lat, lon], get first time slice
slice.mld2 <- st.mld2[,,,1]

# Close nc
nc_close(nc.mld2)

# Create a polygon layer to test intersections
slice.mld.aea.poly2 <-  slice.mld2 |> 
  st_as_sf() |>
  st_union()

# Find intersections (which transects are inside slice.aea.tr)
overlap.mld2 <- st_intersects(survey.transects.sf, slice.mld.aea.poly2, 
                              sparse = FALSE)

# Get the indices of transects that intersect
overlapping.mld_transects2 <- survey.transects.sf[apply(overlap.mld2, 
                                                        1, any), ]

# Get the indices of transects that do not intersect
non_overlapping.mld_transects2 <- survey.transects.sf[!apply(overlap.mld2,
                                                             1, any), ]

# Create file name from device memory
png("mld.regridded_plot_1-step.png", width = 1200, height = 1000, res = 150)

# Check and plot
plot(slice.mld2, col = viridis(100), # Number of colour levels
     main = "Mixing Layer Depth (method: CDO Bilinear (1-step trans.)) - Jan.2020",
     axes = TRUE, reset = FALSE)

# Add Pacific coast and state boundaries
plot(st_geometry(PacificCoast.wgs84 |> 
                   st_transform(crs = st_crs(st.mld2))),
     col = "#E1C699", border = "#ae8f60", lwd = 0.7, add = TRUE)
plot(st_geometry(PCoastStates |>  
                   st_transform(crs = st_crs(st.mld2))),
     col = "#E1C699", border = "#ae8f60", lwd = 0.7, add = TRUE)

# Add city names
coords <- sf::st_coordinates(Populated10)
text(coords[,1], coords[,2], labels = Populated10$name,
     col = "black", pos = 3, cex = 0.8)

# Plot populated places as transects
plot(Populated10, col = "black", pch = 20, cex = 1, add = TRUE)

# Add overlapping and non-overlapping transects
plot(overlapping.mld_transects2, pch = 19, col = "black", cex = 0.5, 
     add = TRUE)
plot(non_overlapping.mld_transects2, pch = 19, col = "red", cex = 0.5, 
     add = TRUE)

dev.off()

```

```{r, structure.data}
# Subfolder for masked output
```

## Find mld intersections

This creates replicate rows for each intersect based on the number of cells intersected in the ROMS output. 

```{r, test.mld.joins}

extract_roms_by_month <- function(f, year_subset) {
  # 1. Load Raster
  r <- terra::rast(f)
  
  # 2. Sync names based on internal time metadata
  r_times <- terra::time(r)
  if(!all(is.na(r_times))) {
    names(r) <- as.character(as.numeric(format(r_times, "%m")))
  } else {
    names(r) <- as.character(1:12) 
  }
  
  # 3. Extract Values
  # Using terra::vect on the year_subset
  v_transects <- terra::vect(year_subset)
  
  # 4. Extract with cells=TRUE to track which grid cell was hit
  # xy=TRUE gives us the center coordinates of the ROMS cell
  ext_raw <- terra::extract(r, v_transects, cells = TRUE, xy = TRUE, 
                            touches = TRUE) 
  
  # 5. Handle the Join safely
  # Instead of row_number(), we rely on the ID column terra::extract creates
  # which corresponds to the row index of v_transects
  year_subset_with_id <- year_subset |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    mutate(temp_ID = seq_len(n()))
  
  # 6. Calculate Diagnostics (Cells per Transect)
  # This counts how many ROMS cells each individual line touched
  diag_counts <- ext_raw |>
    group_by(ID) |>
    summarise(n_cells_intersected = n(), .groups = "drop")
  
  # 7. Merge and Extract
  final_output <- ext_raw |>
    left_join(year_subset_with_id, by = c("ID" = "temp_ID")) |>
    left_join(diag_counts, by = "ID") |>
    # Filter out cases where the point fell outside the raster extent entirely
    filter(!is.na(cell))
  
  # 4. Extract specific month value using matrix indexing
  # We use the Month column from your survey data to pick the right ROMS column
  final_output <- final_output |>
    mutate(
      roms_value = sapply(1:n(), function(i) {
        month_key <- as.character(Month[i])
        if (month_key %in% names(r)) {
          return(.[i, month_key])
        } else {
          return(NA)
        }
      })
    )
  
  # 5. Cleanup and Date Shielding
  final_output <- final_output |>
    # Remove the 12 month columns to keep it tidy
    select(-matches("^[0-9]+$")) |> 
    mutate(
      source_file = basename(f),
      method = "Intersection"
    ) |>
    # Apply the same date-shielding fix as before
    mutate(across(where(~inherits(.x, "POSIXct") || inherits(.x, "IDate") ||
                          inherits(.x, "Date")), as.character))
  
  return(final_output)
}

# --- EXECUTION ---

# Run the parallel process
plan(multisession, workers = 6) # Keep workers low to avoid RAM crash

all_results <- future_lapply(fls, function(f) {
  # Match year from file name
  file_year <- as.numeric(regmatches(f, regexpr("[0-9]{4}", f)))
  
  # TO DO! Upate with the survey transects you wish to use
  year_subset <- survey.transects.sf |> 
    filter(as.numeric(as.character(Year)) == file_year)
  
  if(nrow(year_subset) > 0) {
    return(try(extract_roms_by_month(f, year_subset)))
  } else {
    return(NULL)
  }
}, future.seed = TRUE)

# Filter and Bind
clean_results <- Filter(function(x) !is.null(x) && !inherits(x, "try-error"),
                        all_results)
mld.final_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(clean_results)

# Restore POSIXct Dates
# Replace 'DateColumn' with the actual name in your data
mld.final_table <- mld.final_table |>
  mutate(across(matches("Date|Time"), ~as.POSIXct(.x, tz = "UTC")))

mld.final_table

# Save output
fwrite(mld.final_table, here(dir, "Data", "survey.transects.w.mld.obs.csv"), 
                             sep = ";")

length(unique(mld.final_table$keys))
# [1] 3229

```

```{r, mld.aggregrates}
plotNormalHistogram(mld.final_table$roms_value)

# Check the range of mld depths

mld.final_table.agg <- mld.final_table |>
  group_by(keys) |>
  # Note that this will return NAN values when all values are NA
  ## we want this behaviour because it will tell us which transects have

  summarise(mean_depth = mean(roms_value, na.rm = TRUE), 
            .groups = "keep") |>
  ungroup()
```

## Identify where no intersections exist

For these values, you will need to try bathyemtry or st_nn

```{r, no.intersecting.mld}

# Find which transects do not have a corresponding intersection
no.intersection <-  mld.final_table |>
  group_by(keys) |>
  filter(all(is.na(roms_value))) |>
  ungroup()

# Check that at least one cell intersects
sort(unique(no.intersection$n_cells_intersected))
# [1] 1 2

summary(no.intersection)

```

## For transects without an associated MLD

Here we assign mld based on the nearest feature cell

### Set up the data structure

```{r, data.structure}

# Check column names
colnames(mld.final_table)
#  [1] "ID"                          "cell"                       
#  [3] "x"                           "y"                          
#  [5] "keys"                        "Year"                       
#  [7] "Season"                      "Species_weight"             
#  [9] "len.bin"                     "Bin_Haul_Biomass"           
# [11] "Scaled_Biomass_Contribution" "start_latitude"             
# [13] "start_longitude"             "stop_latitude"              
# [15] "stop_longitude"              "scientific_name"            
# [17] "standard_length"             "date"                       
# [19] "Haul.kg.m3"                  "LenBin.kg.m3"               
# [21] "Country"                     "Bio_Weight_kg"              
# [23] "Fin_sweep.m3"                "Fin_sweep.m2"               
# [25] "lenBin.nb"                   "YearSeas"                   
# [27] "Season.nm"                   "YearSeas.nm"                
# [29] "FID"                         "latBin"                     
# [31] "Present"                     "Haul.kg"                    
# [33] "Haul.check"                  "Haul_Bin.kg"                
# [35] "Month"                       "survey_date"                
# [37] "n_cells_intersected"         "roms_value"                 
# [39] "source_file"                 "method"           

# Save output where there is an intersecting ROMS cell
transects.w.roms.int <- mld.final_table |>
  # Remove cells where there is not at least one intersection
  filter(!keys %in% no.intersection$keys) |>
  # For each unique transect, great a group
  group_by(keys) |>
  # Note that this will return NAN values when all values are NA
  ## we want this behaviour because it will tell us which transects have 
  ## absolutely no intersecting values with ROMS!
  mutate(mean_depth = mean(roms_value, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  mutate(Month = as.character(Month)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # Remove individual cell and fish observations
  select(-c(x, y, ID, cell, source_file, standard_length, 
            Bio_Weight_kg, Scaled_Biomass_Contribution,
            FID, roms_value)) |>
  distinct()

dim(transects.w.roms.int)
# [1] 3316   31

length(unique(transects.w.roms.int$keys))
# [1] 3131

# Filter transects without an intersection
transects.to.run.nn <- survey.transects.sf |>
  filter(keys %in% no.intersection$keys) |>
  # Create a method tag for future reference
  mutate(method = "nngeo::st_nn",
         Month = as.character(Month)
         )

dim(transects.to.run.nn)
# [1] 630    34

length(unique(transects.to.run.nn$keys))
# [1]  118
```

#### Load function and execute

```{r, nn.approach}

# Make sure s2 is on
sf_use_s2(TRUE)

extract_roms_by_month2 <- function(f, year_subset) {
  # 1. Load Raster
  r <- terra::rast(f)

  # 2. Sync Raster Layer Names with internal POSIXct time
  # terra::time(r) returns the POSIXct vector
  r_times <- terra::time(r)
  
  # 2. Sync Raster Layer Names with internal POSIXct time
  # This ensures that names(r) accurately reflects the months in the file
  if(!all(is.na(r_times))) {
    # Extract month (1-12) from the POSIXct metadata
    names(r) <- as.character(as.numeric(format(terra::time(r), "%m")))
  } else {
    names(r) <- as.character(1:12) 
  }
  
  # 3. Handle Annual NA changes
  # Convert to points, dropping cells that are NA for THIS specific year/file
  r_pts <- terra::as.points(r, values = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  r_pts_sf <- st_as_sf(r_pts)
  
  # 4. Nearest Neighbor Search
  # This finds the closest point that HAS data for the current year
  nn_indices <- unlist(nngeo::st_nn(year_subset, r_pts_sf, k = 1, 
                                    progress = FALSE))
  nn_values <- r_pts_sf[nn_indices, ] |> st_drop_geometry()

  # 5. Extraction & Date Protection
  result <- year_subset |>
    mutate(
      roms_value = sapply(1:n(), function(i) {
        month_key <- as.character(Month[i])
        # Safe extraction: check if the month exists in this specific file
        if(month_key %in% names(nn_values)) {
          return(nn_values[i, month_key])
        } else {
          return(NA)
        }
      }),
      source_file = basename(f)
    ) |>
    # SHIELD DATES: Convert POSIXct/IDate to Character to avoid vec_proxy errors
    mutate(across(where(~inherits(.x, "POSIXct") || inherits(.x, "IDate") || inherits(.x, "Date")), as.character))
  
  return(result)
}

# --- EXECUTION ---

# Run the parallel process
plan(multisession, workers = 6) # Keep workers low to avoid RAM crash

all_results2 <- future_lapply(fls, function(f) {
  # Match year from file name
  file_year <- as.numeric(regmatches(f, regexpr("[0-9]{4}", f)))
  
  year_subset <- transects.to.run.nn |> 
    filter(as.numeric(as.character(Year)) == file_year)
  
  if(nrow(year_subset) > 0) {
    return(try(extract_roms_by_month2(f, year_subset)))
  } else {
    return(NULL)
  }
}, future.seed = TRUE)

# Filter and Bind
clean_results <- Filter(function(x) !is.null(x) && !inherits(x, "try-error"), all_results2)
mld.final_table2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(clean_results)

# Restore POSIXct Dates
# Replace 'DateColumn' with the actual name in your data
mld.final_table_w.nn <- mld.final_table2 |>
  mutate(across(matches("Date|Time"), ~as.POSIXct(.x, tz = "UTC")))

mld.final_table_w.nn <- mld.final_table_w.nn |>
  # Remove individual fish observations
  select(-c(source_file, standard_length, Bio_Weight_kg, 
            Scaled_Biomass_Contribution, FID)) |>
  distinct()

```

```{r, final.mld}
  # Rename columns to match intersection data set
  mutate(n_cells_intersected = NA,

  # Remove geometry

  # Drop redundant column
  select(-c(roms_value))

       here(dir, "Data", "mld.final_table_allHistoric.csv"),
```
